questions.stem: A nurse is caring for a client admitted with severe vomiting. Serum potassium is 2.8 mEq/L. Which prescription should the nurse question?

options.rationale: Appropriate nursing action; hypokalemia can cause cardiac dysrhythmias.

options.text: Administer potassium chloride 20 mEq IV push
options.rationale: CORRECT ANSWER TO QUESTION. IV potassium must never be given IV push due to fatal cardiac arrest risk.
Appropriate isotonic fluid support for volume depletion from vomiting.
Appropriate to control vomiting and reduce ongoing electrolyte loss.

questions.educationalObjective: Never administer potassium chloride via IV push; infuse diluted solutions via an infusion pump with cardiac monitoring.

flashcard.front: IV Potassium (KCl) Safety & Hypokalemia ECG Signs
flashcard.back:
• NEVER give IV push/bolus.
• Always infuse via IV pump with appropriate dilution.
• Watch for flattened/inverted T waves, ST depression, prominent U waves.

questions.stem: The nurse assesses a client with hypercalcemia (serum calcium 12.4 mg/dL). Which clinical findings should the nurse expect? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Incorrect. Trousseau and Chvostek signs are classic findings of hypocalcemia.
Correct. Elevated calcium reduces neuromuscular and gastrointestinal motility.

options.text: Flank pain related to renal calculi
options.rationale: Correct. High calcium increases renal stone formation risk.
Incorrect. Hypercalcemia typically causes hypoactive/diminished reflexes.

questions.educationalObjective: Hypercalcemia (>10.5 mg/dL) slows neuromuscular and GI activity and increases risk for kidney stones.

flashcard.back:
• Lethargy, weakness, diminished reflexes.
• Constipation, anorexia, nausea.
• Risk for kidney stones and dysrhythmias.
